- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥1.0) in recent days, model tends to over-forecast, especially after spikes; reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤-1.0) in recent days, model under-forecasts; adjust upward by 3–7% to avoid missing downward momentum.
- Model consistently overestimates 3rd–5th day of forecast horizon after a spike; apply lag correction: subtract 0.5–1.5% per day for days 3–5.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show high volatility or sentiment swing, reduce forecast volatility by 20–30% to reflect mean reversion.
- Forecast horizon 1–3 days: model often misses short-term sentiment-driven reversals; align with sentiment direction, not historical mean.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to overfit recent trend; use 3–5 day moving average to smooth out noise.
